general_guidance: Use clean recycling: empty containers, rinse away residue, and keep paper dry.
GREEN@COMMUNITY accepts nine common recyclable streams. Acceptance differs by material and item construction, so check the official FAQ when the object is composite or uncertain.
Do not infer recyclability from appearance alone. Confirm the material and remove non-recyclable components where practical.

cardboard: Corrugated fibreboard is accepted. Remove plastic tape, paper clips, staples, and other non-paper parts, then keep it dry.
Wet, greasy, or heavily contaminated cardboard may not be suitable for paper recycling.
paper: Newspaper, office paper, books, notes, and corrugated fibreboard are generally accepted after non-paper parts are removed.
Receipts, tracing paper, tissues, hand towels, and photographs are not accepted by GREEN@COMMUNITY.
plastic: Domestic plastic bottles, bags, utensils, containers, packaging, CD cases, and styrofoam are generally accepted after rinsing and emptying.
Rubber, silicone, metal-plastic products, aluminium-lined snack packaging, toothpaste tubes, toothbrushes, and plastic tape are not accepted in the plastic stream.
plastic_container: Empty and rinse plastic bottles, cups, and rigid containers before taking them to GREEN@COMMUNITY.
Separate metal or other non-plastic components where practical. Composite packaging may not be accepted.
plastic_bag_film: Clean domestic plastic bags and non-composite plastic film may be accepted by GREEN@COMMUNITY.
Do not include aluminium-lined snack wrappers, toothpaste tubes, plastic tape, or material whose recyclability is uncertain.
food_organic: Use a participating food-waste collection point or smart food-waste recycling bin where available.
Remove packaging, cutlery, tissues, and other non-food material before depositing food waste.
battery: Portable household rechargeable batteries such as Li-ion, NiMH, and Ni-Cd are accepted at designated collection points. Cover exposed terminals with masking tape first.
Primary batteries, lead-acid batteries, vehicle batteries, and damaged rechargeable batteries require different handling; check the official programme before disposal.
electronic_waste: Regulated electrical equipment and many small household electrical appliances can be delivered through designated recycling channels.
Remove personal data where applicable and do not dismantle devices or place them in ordinary material-recycling bins.
textile: The visual model cannot determine whether a textile is suitable for reuse. Prefer a reputable reuse or textile collection channel when the item is clean and usable.
Wet, contaminated, composite, or damaged textiles may not be accepted; confirm with the collection operator.
foam_disposable_tableware: Clean expanded-polystyrene items and some plastic tableware may be accepted, but food residue and mixed materials can make them unsuitable.
Remove food and non-plastic parts, then confirm acceptance with the selected GREEN@COMMUNITY point.
metal: Tin cans, aluminium cans, clean aluminium foil, and many other metal household items are accepted after rinsing.
Do not place compressed gas cylinders, aerosol cans, chemical containers, non-stick pans, or dangerous sharp items in this stream.
glass: Beverage, food, and sauce glass containers are accepted. Remove caps and rinse before recycling.
Chemical containers, cookware, mirrors, tempered or window glass, ceramics, and crystal are not accepted in glass-container bins.
trash: The visual class 'trash' does not identify the material. Inspect the item for separable paper, plastic, metal, or glass components before disposal.
If the material or acceptance is uncertain, consult the GREEN@COMMUNITY operator instead of contaminating a recycling stream.
general_waste: Check whether the item contains a separately recyclable, rechargeable-battery, or electronic component before treating it as general waste.
If the material is uncertain, ask the collection operator rather than contaminating a recycling stream.

general_guidance: Municipal rules vary. Ask for the city before giving a bin-level instruction.
Official English guidance from Beijing, Shanghai, and Nanjing consistently treats clean and dry paper, plastic, glass, and metal as recyclable waste.
Empty packaging, keep recyclables clean and dry, flatten where appropriate, and wrap sharp or fragile items safely.

cardboard: Clean and dry cardboard is generally recyclable. Flatten large boxes and keep them separate from food residue.
Large pieces may need to be placed neatly beside the recyclable bin or handled through local collection services.
paper: Newspapers, books, paper bags, envelopes, and clean paper packaging are commonly listed as recyclables.
Food-soiled, wet, or composite paper may follow different local rules; confirm with the city guidance.
plastic: Plastic bottles, containers, toys, tubes, hangers, and some foam plastics are listed as recyclable in official city guidance.
Empty and clean packaging first. Composite plastics and heavily contaminated items require local confirmation.
plastic_container: Clean plastic bottles and rigid containers are commonly treated as recyclables, but accepted items vary by city.
Empty and rinse the item, remove obvious non-plastic parts, and follow the local collection rule.
plastic_bag_film: Clean plastic bags or film may be recyclable in some cities, while composite and contaminated film may be residual waste.
Check the city rule before placing flexible plastic in a recyclable bin.
food_organic: Food scraps, grains, vegetables, fruit peel, and similar kitchen waste are commonly treated as household food or wet waste.
Remove all packaging, tissues, and tableware and follow the city's kitchen-waste collection instructions.
battery: Rechargeable, nickel-cadmium, lead-acid, mercury, and button batteries are commonly treated as hazardous waste rather than ordinary recyclables.
Protect exposed terminals and use the city's designated hazardous-waste collection channel.
electronic_waste: Do not place complete electronic devices in ordinary recyclable or residual-waste bins.
Use a standardized electronic-waste recycler or the collection route designated by the city, and remove personal data first.
textile: Clothes, shoes, bags, and other textiles may be considered recyclables in some municipal systems when clean and suitable for recovery.
Reuse is preferable where possible; otherwise confirm the city's collection channel.
foam_disposable_tableware: Foam plastics and disposable tableware must be clean before any recycling route is considered.
Local acceptance differs substantially, so use the city rule when deciding between recyclables and residual waste.
metal: Beverage cans, pots, tools, and other scrap metal are commonly recyclable.
Wrap blades or sharp edges before disposal and follow local hazardous-item instructions where applicable.
glass: Glass bottles, cups, and window glass may be included in recyclable waste, but handling rules differ by city.
Package broken or sharp glass safely before taking it to the locally designated collection point.
trash: The visual class 'trash' is not a disposal category. Identify the material and check whether it belongs to recyclable, hazardous, kitchen/wet, or residual/dry waste.
Ask for the city because household waste categories and accepted collection methods are locally implemented.
general_waste: Treat the prediction as a visual category only and check whether the item is hazardous, food waste, or contains a recyclable component.
Use the city's residual or dry-waste route only after ruling out those special streams.
